rationales: Ernst Haeckel is not credited with introducing the term “prokaryotic.”
Margulis contributed to cell biology but did not coin this term.
Carl Linnaeus developed biological classification, not the term “prokaryotic.”
Édouard Chatton introduced the terms prokaryote and eukaryote.
A.F.A. King is commonly credited with listing about 20 observations supporting the mosquito-malaria connection.
The textbook figure is about 20, not 20? This option gives the reported count.
The reported count is not 30.
The reported count is not 40.
Neurons are generally permanent cells that enter G₀.
Liver cells can enter G₀ but may re-enter the cell cycle when needed.
Kidney cells can enter G₀ and may divide during repair.
Epithelial cells regularly divide and generally do not remain in G₀.
Glycolysis does not occur in the nucleus.
Glycolysis takes place outside the mitochondria.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins and are not the site of glycolysis.
Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm.
A bivalent does not have only two chromatids; it comprises two duplicated homologous chromosomes.
A bivalent has four chromatids, not three.
A bivalent consists of two homologous chromosomes, each with two chromatids, for a total of four.
A bivalent has four chromatids, not eight.
Houbara bustards migrate to Pakistan during winter.
They do not make this migration in summer.
Autumn is not the season in which they arrive for their wintering period.
Spring is not the season in which they migrate to Pakistan for winter.
Stomata cover roughly 1–2% of a leaf’s surface.
Four to five percent is greater than the usual textbook estimate.
Eight to nine percent is much greater than the usual estimate.
Ten to twenty percent is much greater than the usual estimate.
Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis.
Crossing over does not take place during metaphase I.
Crossing over does not take place during anaphase I.
Crossing over does not take place during telophase I.
Hydrogen makes up about 10% of protoplasm, not 65%.
Hydrogen makes up about 10%, not 18%.
Hydrogen makes up about 10% of protoplasm.
Hydrogen makes up about 10%, not 3%.
G₁ is mainly a growth phase before DNA replication.
In G₂, the cell makes proteins needed for mitosis, including spindle-related proteins.
S phase is when DNA is replicated.
G₀ is a resting state outside the active cell cycle.
Malaria is not caused by bacteria.
Malaria is not caused by a virus.
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites.
Amoeba is not the parasite that causes malaria.
Chitin is a major component of fungal cell walls, not plant cell walls.
Peptidoglycan is found in bacterial cell walls.
Cellulose is the major structural component of plant cell walls.
Cholesterol is not the major component of plant cell walls.
Plant cells have cell walls, usually made mainly of cellulose.
Animal cells lack cell walls.
Bacteria generally have cell walls, commonly containing peptidoglycan.
Fungi have cell walls, commonly containing chitin.
Amoeba is a unicellular organism, not a colonial one.
Paramecium is unicellular rather than colonial.
Euglena is generally unicellular rather than colonial.
Volvox is a classic example of a colonial organism.
Lipase does not act on carbohydrates.
Lipase does not act on proteins.
Lipase acts on lipids, breaking them down.
Lipase does not act on nucleic acids.
